subject: Climate & Environment
title: How Many Species Exist
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on How Many Species Exist.

hook.text: Scientists have described about 2 million species. The real number may be 8 to 10 million.

buildup.text: New species are discovered every week — about 18,000 per year, mostly insects and fungi.

discovery.text: The deep ocean, soil, and tropical canopy are least explored. They hold the most unknowns.

twist.text: We may lose species to extinction faster than we can discover and name them.

climax.text: Cataloging life on Earth is a race against time — and science is losing.

punchline.text: We share the planet with millions of neighbors we've never met.

quiz.question: How many species are estimated to exist on Earth?

details.summary: Scientists have described roughly 2 million species, but estimates of total species on Earth range from 8 to 12 million, with some models suggesting far more. Insects, fungi, and deep-sea organisms remain vastly undercounted, meaning many species may vanish before being discovered.
details.whyItMatters: We cannot protect what we have not found. The immense gap between known and estimated species reveals the true scale of what we risk losing.
takeaways: About 2 million species have been formally described so far
Total estimates range from 8 million to over 12 million species
Most unknown species are insects, fungi, and marine invertebrates

faq.question: Why is it so hard to count all species on Earth?
faq.answer: Many species live in remote, inaccessible habitats like deep oceans, tropical canopies, and soil. Others are tiny or cryptic and require genetic analysis to distinguish. Funding and taxonomic expertise also limit the pace of discovery.

faq.question: How many species go extinct before being discovered?
faq.answer: Estimates suggest thousands of species disappear each year before science describes them, particularly in tropical forests being rapidly cleared. We lose both the species and the knowledge of their ecological roles.
